title: The Nile IS Just a River in Egypt
summary: Josh and Chuck open with a Kiva shout-out (the team has passed $700,000 in loans), then explore the Nile River: its ten to eleven countries, the disputed source (Lake Victoria versus headwaters in a Rwandan forest, with John Hanning Speke's claims), the White and Blue Niles, the Victoria and Albert Nile names, the Great Bend, the six cataracts, the Delta and its distributaries, the annual flood and silt that fed ancient Egypt, dams and fertilizer, Egypt and Sudan water politics, Nile crocodiles including Gustav, hippos, malaria and travel health, the Aswan dam, and the Nile's population density. The episode closes with listener mail from Eli in Minnesota and a request for autumn recipes.

segments.title: Opening banter and Kiva shout-out
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the show and give a Kiva shout-out, noting the team has reached $700,000 in loans and is on track for its goal.

segments.title: Gustav the crocodile
segments.summary: The hosts introduce Gustav, a huge old Nile crocodile blamed for about 300 deaths, and the hunter Patrese Faye who pursued him. They say the man-eating legends are probably exaggerated.

segments.title: Countries and width of the Nile
segments.summary: The hosts list the countries the Nile flows through, note its width of up to ten kilometers, and say about 370 million people depend on it. They mention Ethiopia's role in ancient history.

segments.title: Nile length and the source debate
segments.summary: The hosts compare the Nile's length with the Amazon's and describe John Hanning Speke's claim that Lake Victoria was the source. Later expeditions located the headwaters south of Lake Victoria in a forest in Rwanda, so the Nile flows south to north.

segments.title: White Nile, Blue Nile and tributaries
segments.summary: The hosts describe the White Nile and Blue Nile, the Victoria, Albert and Nile names along the river, and the Atbara River, which they say was once the original source. They also cover the splitting of the river in Egypt into the Damietta and Rosetta distributaries.

segments.title: Cataracts, the Great Bend and the Nile's course
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the six cataracts between Aswan and the Delta, the Nile's sharp bend through the Sahara, and the desert's role as natural protection for Egypt.

segments.title: Annual flood, silt and ancient Egypt
segments.summary: The hosts explain the Nile's seasonal rise and fall, the flood (inundation) that deposited fertile silt, and how ancient Egyptians captured water for crops. They also cover the problems of floods and the later move to dams and fertilizer.

segments.title: Nile water politics and dams
segments.summary: The hosts discuss water-sharing disputes among Egypt, Sudan and Ethiopia and the Nile Basin Initiative, plus Egypt's blocking of projects. They also describe the nilometer and the Aswan dam, which opened in 1970.

segments.title: Wildlife, health tips and closing
segments.summary: The hosts talk about hippos, malaria and travel precautions, and modern farming along the Nile. They say the Amazon will be covered in a future show.

segments.title: Listener mail from Eli in Minnesota
segments.summary: Eli, a fourteen-year-old listener from Lindstrom, Minnesota, writes in praising the show and mentions his scoutmaster Dana. The hosts ask for autumn treat recipes and close with a plug for the video podcast.
